overview: This single-page file consists of a register or index sheet recording two July 1936 communications from the U.S. Consulate at Taihoku concerning the official observance of American Independence Day. Both entries describe the consular response to a congratulatory address delivered by the Director General of Taiwan at a July 4 reception; one also notes a specimen invitation and translated newspaper coverage. The sheet appears to be a filing aid rather than the underlying despatches or their enclosures.

subfiles.title: Register sheet for Taihoku reports on the 1936 Independence Day reception
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes two Taihoku communications about the July 4, 1936 official reception and the response to the Director General of Taiwan's congratulatory address.
subfiles.summary: The first entry, dated July 8, records a copy of the response to the Director General's address and mentions a specimen invitation and material translated from newspapers. The second, dated July 7, reports the observance of Independence Day and encloses the same or a closely related response. The page is an administrative summary of those communications rather than the communications themselves.

interest: The sheet offers compact evidence of ceremonial relations between American consular officers and Taiwan's Japanese colonial administration in 1936. Its paired entries reveal how a single diplomatic occasion generated both formal reporting and supporting ephemera, including an invitation and translated press coverage. It is also useful for identifying underlying documents and enclosures that may survive elsewhere, despite the discrepancy between the file title and the number printed on the page.
